did: Made each some-ui pull request cost fewer of the runners both repositories share. The eleven repo-wide guards now run as one job, so a push starts 14 jobs instead of 24, and the guards take 2 billed minutes instead of about 20. A draft pull request now runs nothing until it is marked ready, and shows a red gate meanwhile. I also measured where the waiting came from: about 20 jobs at once is the cap, and the server's PR gate holds one runner for up to an hour while it waits.

calls.title: What a draft pull request shows when its CI is skipped
options: the gate fails, so a draft shows a red check until it is ready
the gate is skipped, so a draft shows no failure
drafts keep running all of CI
calls.why: A skipped required check counts as passed, and when a draft is marked ready its old gate is the only one on that commit until the new run reaches it, so a skip could let it merge unchecked.
calls.undo: Drop ready_for_review and the draft conditions from pr.yml, extension.yml and pages.yml (call C43).

left: The server's PR gate still holds a runner while it waits on the other checks; the event-driven fix is server issue 762, filed by the coordinator, because this session could not push to the server.
Whether a merge queue is offered on these repositories is unknown: the docs don't say, so issue 2824 asks for a one-minute look at the ruleset's rule list.
magic-nix-cache sometimes spends minutes saving the Nix toolchain to a pull request's own cache; the action has no read-only mode, so it was left on.
